articles.title: Oleshky: How is the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city going?
articles.summary: Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson explains the temporary ceasefire in the devastated town of Oleshky.
articles.body:
Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky were evacuated and driven to safety on Friday, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

Residents had a four-hour window to leave the city. Some people are understood to have stayed despite the lack of power and water in the area.

The BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson explains how the ceasefire is going and what could happen next.

articles.title: Tráfico de drogas em Piraí: dupla é presa com carga na RJ-145 | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu na altura do km 27 da rodovia.
articles.summary: Durante fiscalização na RJ-145, o BPRv prendeu dois homens que transportavam entorpecentes para Vassouras, Valença e Barra do Piraí em um veículo de carga.
articles.body:
Dupla é presa suspeita de tráfico de drogas na RJ-145, em Piraí — Foto: Divulgação/BPRv

Dois homens foram presos por suspeita de tráfico de drogas nesta sexta-feira (30) na RJ-145, em Piraí (RJ). O caso aconteceu na altura do km 27.

Segundo o BPRv, os agentes estavam em uma fiscalização de rotina na rodovia, quando abordaram um veículo de carga acompanhado de um "batedor".

Ainda de acordo com o BPRv, durante a abordagem, foi realizada uma busca pelo veículo de carga, onde foram encontradas uma grande quantidade de drogas.

O BPRv também informou que a drogas tinham como destino as cidades de Vassouras (RJ), Valença (RJ) e Barra do Piraí (RJ).

Os suspeitos e todo material apreendido foram encaminhados para a delegacia de Piraí, onde o caso foi registrado.

Eles permaneceram presos e à disposição da Justiça.

A identidade deles não foi divulgada pela BPRv.

articles.title: Ruas do Parque dos Poderes serão fechadas no feriado de Finados | G1
articles.standfirst: Espaço ficará liberado para pedestres e ciclistas de sábado (31) até segunda-feira (2). Equipes do Detran-MS vão fiscalizar o trânsito na região.
articles.summary: Espaço ficará liberado para pedestres e ciclistas de sábado (31) até segunda-feira (2). Equipes do Detran-MS vão fiscalizar o trânsito na região.
articles.body:
Acesso às vias do Parque dos Poderes ficará exclusivo a pedestres e ciclistas. — Foto: Governo de MS

As ruas do Parque dos Poderes, em Campo Grande , ficarão fechadas para veículos de sábado (31) até segunda-feira (2), durante o feriado prolongado de Finados.

A medida faz parte do projeto Amigos do Parque e tem como objetivo garantir mais segurança para quem utiliza o espaço para caminhadas, passeios de bicicleta e atividades físicas.

Durante os três dias, apenas pedestres e ciclistas poderão circular pelas vias interditadas. Equipes do Departamento Estadual de Trânsito de Mato Grosso do Sul (Detran-MS) vão controlar o tráfego e fiscalizar a região para garantir a segurança dos frequentadores.

O fechamento das ruas faz parte do projeto Amigos do Parque, que restringe a circulação de veículos aos sábados, domingos e feriados para incentivar o lazer e a prática de esportes ao ar livre.

O Parque dos Poderes é uma das áreas de Campo Grande que preservam a vegetação nativa. O local é bastante frequentado por moradores, principalmente nos fins de semana, para caminhadas, corridas e passeios de bicicleta.

articles.title: Incêndio em Capanema: família é sepultada após 59 dias da tragédia | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher e duas crianças foram enterradas em cerimônia reservada a familiares e amigos. Exame de DNA para identificação da quarta vítima foi inconclusivo, segundo a Polícia Científica.
articles.summary: Após 59 dias, mãe e filhos mortos no incêndio em Capanema foram sepultados, enquanto a identificação do corpo do pai aguarda novos resultados de exames de DNA.
articles.body:
Três das quatro vítimas do incêndio que atingiu uma loja e matou integrantes de uma mesma família em Capanema, no nordeste do Pará, foram sepultadas após 59 dias da tragédia. O enterro ocorreu na quinta-feira (29), em uma cerimônia reservada a familiares e amigos próximos. O corpo da quarta vítima ainda aguarda confirmação da identidade por exame de DNA.

Foram sepultados Charlene Dieli Damaceno de Araújo, de 35 anos, e os filhos José Pietro, de 10 anos, e Maria Valentina, de 8 anos.

A família havia divulgado uma nota pedindo que não houvesse aglomeração durante o velório e o sepultamento. O pedido foi respeitado, e não houve manifestações públicas durante a despedida.

O corpo do empresário José Ribeiro Soares, de 48 anos, não foi sepultado junto com as outras vítimas porque a identificação por DNA ainda não foi concluída.

Em nota, a Polícia Científica do Pará informou que o exame de identificação genética foi inconclusivo. Novas amostras de familiares foram coletadas, e os exames estão em andamento.

O incêndio ocorreu na noite de 5 de setembro, por volta das 22h, em um prédio de três andares no bairro São José, em Capanema.

No térreo funcionava uma loja de peças e acessórios automotivos, enquanto os dois andares superiores eram usados como residência pela família.

Família é vítima de incêndio em Capanema, no Pará. — Foto: Reprodução / TV Liberal

O fogo começou na parte inferior do imóvel e se espalhou rapidamente. No estabelecimento havia pneus e outros materiais inflamáveis.

Durante o incêndio, os quatro integrantes da família ficaram presos em um cômodo no terceiro andar. Eles chegaram a usar as lanternas dos celulares e gritar por socorro na tentativa de chamar a atenção de moradores e equipes de resgate.

Apesar das tentativas de salvamento feitas por moradores e pelo Corpo de Bombeiros, as quatro vítimas morreram carbonizadas.

articles.title: Why is Netanyahu accusing Palestinian Israeli parties of fraud?

articles.body:
The votes have been counted in Israel’s general election and there is no overall majority.

Benjamin Netanyahu has accused Palestinian Israeli parties of “stealing” the polls and accepting funding from Qatar to do it.

Those parties have denied wrongdoing, the Electoral Commission has found no evidence of fraud and Qatar denies any involvement.

So, is this a way for Netanyahu to stop Palestinian Israeli parties from forming a coalition with the opposition to unseat his Likud party?

articles.summary: Participantes vão se concentrar na Praça Prefeito Tarcísio Delgado. Cantora gospel Rose Nascimento é uma das atrações.
articles.body:
Marcha é realizada pela Ordem Estadual dos Ministros Evangélicos de Roraima — Foto: Omer/Divulgação

A Marcha para Jesus vai provocar alterações no trânsito do Centro de Juiz de Fora neste sábado (31). A programação começa às 14h, na Praça Prefeito Tarcísio Delgado, com apresentações de bandas e ministérios locais.

Às 16h, os participantes sairão em marcha pelas avenidas Itamar Franco e Rio Branco, com retorno pela Getúlio Vargas até a Praça Prefeito Tarcísio Delgado.

Durante a passagem dos participantes, o trânsito terá as seguintes alterações:

Avenida Itamar Franco : circulação em meia pista, no sentido Centro, entre as avenidas Getúlio Vargas e Rio Branco

Avenida Rio Branco : interdição da pista lateral, no sentido Manoel Honório, entre as avenidas Itamar Franco e Getúlio Vargas

Avenida Getúlio Vargas : interdição da faixa da esquerda, destinada a carros de passeio, entre as avenidas Rio Branco e Itamar Franco.

A marcha terminará na Praça Prefeito Tarcísio Delgado, de onde os participantes sairão. Não há previsão de desvios nas linhas de ônibus, já que o trânsito será liberado após a passagem dos fiéis.

Agentes da Secretaria de Mobilidade Urbana (SMU) estarão no local para orientar os motoristas e organizar o trânsito durante o evento.

A partir das 18h, haverá novas apresentações musicais. Às 20h, a cantora gospel Rose Nascimento sobe ao palco.

articles.title: Jovem internado por 75 dias recebe 'visita' de moto: 'Queria muito' | G1
articles.standfirst: Familiares levaram o veículo até o hospital. Ação foi sugerida por médicos para ajudar na reabilitação.
articles.summary: Familiares levaram o veículo até o hospital. Ação foi sugerida por médicos para ajudar na reabilitação.
articles.body:
O agrônomo João Marcelo, de 24 anos, recebeu uma visita inusitada após cerca de 75 dias internado na UTI, em Formosa , no Entorno do Distrito Federal, a moto dele. João foi hospitalizado com pancreatite, segundo os médicos. Ele disse que "queria muito" rever a motocicleta.

João pratica motocross e os médicos acreditavam que sair do isolamento e ver algo familiar poderia ajudar na reabilitação. Eles então perguntaram o que o jovem gostaria de ver.

"Sempre perguntam o que a gente sente, o que a gente quer. Eu falei: 'Moça, eu queria muito a minha moto. Antes de eu morrer eu quero a minha moto'", disse João.

Os amigos e familiares se juntaram para levar a moto até o hospital. Depois, a equipe médica se mobilizou para levar o paciente ainda na maca até o veículo.

O médico Oliver Vilanova contou que o esforço do paciente para acelerar a motocicleta ficou gravado em sua memória. "Sem dúvida, isso foi um fator que contribuiu muito para a melhora dele e apoio à família", disse.

O esforço deu certo, pois João recebeu alta dias depois da visita. Atualmente, ele continua fazendo fisioterapia, mas afirmou que já tem planos para depois da recuperação.

"[Voltar] a andar, quando eu estiver 100%, e realizar meu casamento que agora está parado. Dar valor nas pessoas que está com você. É só as pessoas que gostam de você e realmente amam para estar com você", concluiu João.

Ao g1 , Emely Engler, noiva de João, explicou que, antes de ser internado, ele estava vomitando e sem fome. Ela disse que João procurou o hospital com um quadro de desidratação e fraqueza, mas acabou tendo uma parada cardíaca e precisou ser entubado.

"Ele teve uma pancreatite, que levou a tudo isso. Hoje ele está bem melhor. Conversa normalmente, entende tudo, porém ainda está acamado, pois não consegue caminhar", disse Emely.

A noiva do agrônomo destacou que, com as fisioterapias, ele já consegue se sentar e deitar sozinho, e que as conquistas continuam à medida que o tratamento avança.

articles.title: Secretário promete ampliar tecnologia e combate a facções no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Confirmado no comando da Segurança Pública para o próximo mandato, Antônio Luiz defendeu investimentos em tecnologia, integração entre instituições e fortalecimento das ações de inteligência.
articles.summary: Mantido no cargo durante o próximo mandato de Rafael, Antônio Luiz defendeu investimentos em tecnologia, integração entre instituições e fortalecimento das ações de inteligência.
articles.body:
Confirmado pelo governador reeleito Rafael Fonteles (PT) para permanecer à frente da Secretaria de Segurança Pública do Piauí pelos próximos quatro anos, Antônio Luiz afirmou nesta quinta-feira (29) que pretende ampliar o uso de tecnologia no policiamento e fortalecer ações de combate às facções criminosas.

Em entrevista à TV Clube , o secretário destacou que a política de integração entre as forças de segurança será mantida e citou investimentos em inteligência e inovação tecnológica como pilares da estratégia para o próximo mandato.

Segundo ele, o modelo adotado no estado contribuiu para a redução dos indicadores de criminalidade e serviu de referência para outras unidades da federação e para o governo federal.

Entre os investimentos, está a ampliação do sistema de videomonitoramento inteligente já utilizado em Teresina , no Norte e no litoral. Segundo Antônio Luiz, a expectativa é expandir a cobertura para municípios como Picos, Floriano e Piripiri.

"Vamos investir mais em tecnologia. Hoje temos as câmeras do SPIA em Teresina e na região Norte do estado. Precisamos ampliar essa cobertura para outras cidades", disse.

De acordo com Antônio Luiz, as ferramentas tecnológicas ajudam a identificar suspeitos e monitorar deslocamentos após a prática de crimes.

Integração com Judiciário e Ministério Público

O secretário também defendeu uma atuação mais integrada entre as forças de segurança, o Judiciário e o Ministério Público do Piauí para ampliar a efetividade do combate à criminalidade.

Segundo ele, muitos criminosos considerados de alta periculosidade acabam sendo colocados em liberdade enquanto ainda respondem a outros processos.

"Precisamos de um trabalho mais integrado para que haja mais rapidez nos processos e no acompanhamento desses criminosos", afirmou.

Durante a entrevista, Antônio Luiz defendeu alterações na legislação penal para crimes considerados graves.

Ele afirmou apoiar a redução da maioridade penal para crimes hediondos e também mudanças no Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente (ECA) para ampliar o período de internação de adolescentes envolvidos em atos infracionais graves.

Antônio Luiz foi o primeiro integrante do secretariado anunciado por Rafael Fonteles para o mandato que começa em janeiro de 2027.

No mesmo dia, o governador também confirmou a permanência do secretário estadual de Saúde, Dirceu Campelo. Os demais nomes da futura equipe devem ser anunciados nas próximas semanas.

articles.title: Facilities no Brasil: o setor invisível que mantém as empresas funcionando | G1
articles.standfirst: De serviço de apoio a estratégia de gestão: como a administração de ambientes, pessoas e rotinas se tornou um dos pilares da produtividade nas empresas brasileira.
articles.summary: De serviço de apoio a estratégia de gestão: como a administração de ambientes, pessoas e rotinas se tornou um dos pilares da produtividade nas empresas brasileira.
articles.body:
Quando tudo funciona, ninguém percebe. A recepção acolhe o visitante, o prédio está limpo, o acesso é controlado, o ar-condicionado funciona, o elevador não para, a copa está abastecida. É justamente essa sensação de normalidade que define o bom facilities: um conjunto de serviços que sustenta a rotina de uma empresa sem aparecer, e que só ganha destaque quando falha.

No Brasil, esse setor deixou de ser tratado como coadjuvante e passou a ocupar um lugar na mesa de decisões.

A palavra vem do inglês e se refere ao conjunto de serviços de apoio que garantem o funcionamento de um espaço e das pessoas que o utilizam. O chamado facility management, ou gestão de facilities, integra e coordena essas atividades para que a empresa possa concentrar energia no que realmente é seu negócio.

Entre os serviços que costumam fazer parte do portfólio estão:

Manutenção predial (elétrica, hidráulica, ar-condicionado, elevadores)

Algumas mudanças explicam o avanço do facilities no país:

1.Foco no core business. Empresas perceberam que não precisam gerir diretamente serviços que não fazem parte da sua atividade principal, e passaram a terceirizá-los a parceiros especializados.

2.Busca por eficiência. Gerir vários fornecedores separados gera retrabalho, desencontro de informações e custos escondidos. Integrar os serviços simplifica a gestão.

3.Experiência de quem usa o espaço. Colaboradores, clientes e visitantes avaliam a empresa também pelo ambiente: limpeza, acolhimento, conforto e organização influenciam percepção e produtividade.

4.Exigências de conformidade. Normas trabalhistas, de segurança do trabalho, sanitárias e ambientais pedem processos documentados e fornecedores regulares.

5.Novos modelos de trabalho. Escritórios híbridos, espaços compartilhados e operações logísticas em expansão exigem flexibilidade e dimensionamento inteligente dos serviços.

Apesar da tecnologia, o facilities é, em essência, um negócio de pessoas. Vigilantes, recepcionistas, auxiliares de limpeza, técnicos de manutenção e supervisores formam a linha de frente que o cliente vê todos os dias. Por isso, alguns fatores pesam mais do que o preço:

Baixa rotatividade, que preserva o conhecimento sobre o local.

Liderança próxima, com supervisão presente e canal direto com o cliente.

Cultura de valorização, que reflete na qualidade do atendimento.

A gestão de facilities também vem incorporando recursos que mudaram a forma de operar:

Plataformas de gestão que registram chamados, rondas, ocorrências e checklists.

Monitoramento e controle de acesso eletrônico;

Indicadores de desempenho (SLA) que permitem acompanhar a qualidade do serviço de forma objetiva.

Práticas de sustentabilidade, como gestão de resíduos, uso racional de recursos e produtos de menor impacto ambiental.

Com dados, o facilities deixa de ser reativo (“resolver o problema quando acontece”) e passa a ser preventivo e estratégico.

Nem tudo é simples. O mercado brasileiro convive com desafios que exigem maturidade dos fornecedores e atenção dos contratantes:

Alta rotatividade em funções operacionais.

Competição por preço, que pode levar à queda de qualidade e a riscos trabalhistas.

Complexidade regulatória, com regras que variam por atividade e por região.

Necessidade de padronização em empresas com unidades em diferentes cidades.

Demanda por qualificação, tanto técnica quanto comportamental.

Os fornecedores que conseguem enfrentar esses pontos com processos claros, treinamento e transparência tendem a construir contratos mais longos e relações mais sólidas.

Com mais de 55 anos de atuação, a SEGVAP acompanhou a transformação do setor, de serviços isolados à gestão integrada de facilities. A empresa trabalha com a premissa de que segurança, recepção, limpeza e demais serviços de apoio devem funcionar de forma coordenada, com diagnóstico, protocolos, equipes capacitadas e acompanhamento contínuo de resultados.

Para o cliente, isso significa menos pontas soltas, um único parceiro responsável pela qualidade e mais tempo para cuidar do que realmente importa: o próprio negócio.

Bom facilities é aquele que ninguém percebe, porque tudo simplesmente funciona.

A tendência é de ainda mais integração entre serviços, uso de dados na tomada de decisão, foco em sustentabilidade e em experiência de quem ocupa os espaços. Empresas que enxergam o facilities como parte da estratégia, e não como custo de rotina, ganham eficiência, previsibilidade e uma operação mais preparada para crescer.

articles.title: Funcionários do Theatro Municipal contam casos sobrenaturais | G1
articles.standfirst: Funcionários contam histórias de espectros, fumaça negra e até torneira que abre sozinha. Visita inspirada nos 'fantasmas' do teatro acontece desde 2023.
articles.summary: Com ingressos esgotados em minutos, a Visita Fantasma no Theatro Municipal apresenta relatos reais de aparições e fenômenos vividos por funcionários no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
Às vésperas do Dia das Bruxas, funcionários do Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro contaram ao RJ2 relatos de casos sobrenaturais vividos no local.

Entre as histórias estão casos de aparições de funcionários que já morreram, uma fumaça negra sufocadora, instrumentos tocando sozinho, espectos, entre outras (veja detalhes mais adiante na reportagem).

Aproveitando esse histórico, o teatr promove a “Visita Fantasma”, atração inspirada nos relatos sobrenaturais de funcionários do teatro centenário. A visita é organizada desde 2023, especialmente nesse período do ano.

A sessão para adultos acontece nesta sexta-feira (30), à noite. Neste sábado (31), a visita é voltada ao público infantil, em dois horários pela manhã: às 10h e às 11h30.

Segundo a chefe de gabinete do teatro, Bárbara Ottero, a procura é grande: "Quando a gente anuncia venda, esgota em dois minutos, quatro no máximo, acho que nunca passou de quatro minutos, porque as pessoas têm muita curiosidade".

O RJ2 ouviu funcionários que dizem ter vivido experiências inexplicáveis no prédio.

O baixo do coro Pedro Olivero conta que era amigo de Carmen, chefe das camareiras do Theatro Municipal, que morreu atropelada ao sair de uma igreja em Salvador. Segundo ele, um ano depois, ao atravessar o palco a caminho do banheiro, cumprimentou a camareira, que respondeu normalmente. Só depois percebeu que ela já havia morrido.

“Não fiquei assustado, porque ela era uma pessoa querida", ele relata. "Eu gostei de ter visto a Carmen. Fiquei muito feliz”.

O barítono Fábio Belizzalo, que integra o coro desde 1994, relata ter visto, ao fim de um ensaio, uma figura branca e flutuante que cantava como um soprano. Segundo ele, o espectro atravessou a passarela do prédio anexo, chegou ao palco e desapareceu.

Funcionários do Theatro Municipal contam que já ouviram piano tocar sozinho — Foto: Reprodução/RJ2

Ele diz que o professor de canto, seu D’Ângelo, de 92 anos, também viu a cena. Menos de um ano depois, o professor morreu, e Fábio afirma que passou a vê-lo no camarote durante ensaios de “Aida”. O barítono diz ainda que, certa manhã, ouviu o piano tocar sozinho em uma sala trancada. Sobre as experiências, afirma: “É um privilégio poder ver e ouvir”.

A chefe de gabinete do Theatro, Bárbara Ottero, que se diz agnóstica, conta que viu a torneira de um banheiro do balcão nobre abrir sozinha durante um velório.

"Levo pelo menos no bom humor quando acontece, mas tem muita gente que tem medo de ir embora à tarde e de madrugada, então eu com certeza não sou única. Eu acho que a minha vivência foi a mais leve possível".

Ela também relata que uma equipe de um prédio vizinho dizia sofrer com portas batendo e objetos caindo, e que a equipe do teatro chegou a “conversar com os espíritos”. Durante os ensaios da visita fantasma, inclusive, uma museóloga fotografou uma pessoa parada em um corredor, segundo Bárbara.

Alberto da Silva conta que foi surpreendido por fumaça negra sufocadora no Theatro Municipal — Foto: Reprodução/RJ2

O eletricista Alberto da Silva, mais conhecido como Beto, trabalha há 32 anos no teatro. Ele afirma que, entre 1996 e 1997, descansava em um camarim quando uma fumaça negra entrou pela porta de veneziana e tomou a forma de um animal parecido com um gorila.

Segundo ele, a forma o sufocou, e só desapareceu quando ele conseguiu gritar “Jesus!”. “Nunca mais voltei para ficar descansando aqui”, conta.

A assessora da presidência Helene Nascimento conta que, há cerca de dez anos, viu um homem de fraque entrar em um andar já vazio, à noite. Ela diz que o seguiu pelos ambientes do teatro, mas ele desapareceu.

“Todo mundo aqui tem uma história, seja lá corpo artístico, o balé, coro, orquestra ou até mesmo os técnicos, todo mundo tem uma história, tem uma vivência”, relata.

A “Visita Fantasma” é uma visita guiada pelo teatro. O ator Caetano Cardinot interpreta um médium que ajuda o público a descobrir quais fantasmas estarão presentes na edição especial. Segundo a organização, as histórias foram reunidas em pesquisas em jornais e arquivos e nos relatos de funcionários.

“O grande protagonista é o teatro, então cada um desses pilares vai nos revelar alguns segredos para que a gente possa, no fim, descobrir quem, além de nós, visita esse espaço”, explica Caetano.

O ator diz que tem “muito respeito pelos espíritos”, mas admite: “Eu sou um pouco medroso”.

articles.standfirst: Unidade revitalizada reúne novas marcas, ambientes reestruturados e programação especial até domingo (01/11), em Curitiba.
articles.summary: Unidade revitalizada reúne novas marcas, ambientes reestruturados e programação especial até domingo (01/11), em Curitiba.
articles.body:
A possibilidade de encontrar ingredientes especiais, experimentar novos sabores e descobrir alternativas para diferentes hábitos alimentares faz parte da experiência do novo Supermercados Ítalo, no bairro do Portão, em Curitiba. A unidade reabriu nesta quinta-feira (29/10) com uma nova área de destaque, a Padaria Sem Glúten do Grupo Ítalo, collabs com marcas locais, cafés especiais, uma adega renovada e uma seleção ampliada de produtos nacionais e importados. Faça um tour no Ítalo Portão .

Para apresentar as novidades, o supermercado preparou uma programação especial até domingo, 1º de novembro. Durante o período, os clientes poderão participar de ações especiais e degustações em loja, em uma oportunidade para conhecer os novos ambientes e as opções que passam a integrar a unidade. Confira aqui mais novidades do Ítalo Portão .

Presente no bairro desde 2020, o Ítalo Portão passou por uma revitalização completa. A transformação faz parte de um movimento do Grupo Ítalo para acompanhar a evolução da região e oferecer um ambiente que combine as compras do cotidiano com novas possibilidades de alimentação, conveniência e gastronomia.

Padaria sem glúten amplia as opções de alimentação

Uma das principais novidades é a segunda Padaria Sem Glúten do Grupo Ítalo. A primeira foi inaugurada no Ítalo Barigui e ampliou as alternativas para consumidores que procuram produtos sem glúten. Agora, a proposta chega também ao Portão, incorporando ao supermercado uma opção para quem possui restrições alimentares ou simplesmente deseja conhecer outras possibilidades de consumo. Veja como funciona a Padaria sem Glúten do Ítalo .

A padaria sem glúten é a segunda do Grupo Ítalo e significa alimentos e produtos livres de glúten e essenciais para quem precisa. — Foto: Divulgação/Ítalo.

A expansão desse espaço acompanha a atenção crescente dos consumidores à composição dos alimentos e à diversidade de produtos disponíveis. Com a nova padaria, o Ítalo amplia o acesso a esse tipo de produto em mais uma unidade da rede.

A gastronomia também ganhou espaço por meio de parcerias com marcas especializadas. A proposta é reunir, no mesmo endereço, produtos e experiências que ampliam as possibilidades de escolha dos consumidores.

Entre as collabs está o Taisho Grab & Go , que oferece culinária japonesa pronta para levar. A Cipria acrescenta ao mix especiarias e temperos selecionados, ingredientes que permitem explorar combinações de sabores e diversificar o preparo de receitas em casa. Já a Trapiche Pescados amplia a oferta de peixes e frutos do mar, produtos que fazem parte de diferentes tradições culinárias e podem compor desde refeições cotidianas até ocasiões especiais.

Outra parceria é com a Zenite , especializada em alimentos funcionais, que acrescenta alternativas para consumidores interessados em diversificar a alimentação. As quatro collabs contribuem para ampliar a variedade da unidade e aproximar os clientes de produtos e especialidades que nem sempre fazem parte das compras habituais.

O supermercado também renovou a adega e ampliou a seleção de produtos nacionais e importados. Os cafés especiais completam as novidades, oferecendo novas marcas em seu mix de produtos para quem aprecia diferentes origens e perfis de bebidas.

O Ítalo Portão passou por uma transformação total para atender as necessidades dos consumidores da região. — Foto: Divulgação/Supermercados Ítalo.

Ítalo Gourmet integra a experiência gastronômica

A unidade conta ainda com o restaurante Ítalo Gourmet, que oferece almoço diariamente, das 11h às 15h. O restaurante foi remodelado e segue como alternativas para quem trabalha ou circula pelo bairro e procura um espaço de qualidade para fazer a refeição.

A presença do restaurante, somada às marcas parceiras e à variedade de produtos, reforça a proposta de reunir diferentes experiências gastronômicas em um único local. Assim, a visita ao supermercado pode incluir desde a escolha de ingredientes para cozinhar em casa até uma refeição pronta.

Renovação acompanha a história do supermercado no Portão

A transformação da unidade também representa a continuidade de uma relação construída com os moradores desde 2020. Ao longo dos últimos seis anos, o Ítalo passou a integrar a rotina do bairro, acompanhando as necessidades de consumidores que utilizam o supermercado em diferentes momentos do dia.

Segundo Edy João Dal Berto, presidente do Grupo Ítalo, a revitalização procura justamente acompanhar as mudanças da região sem perder a proximidade com os clientes.

“Estamos muito felizes em revitalizar o Ítalo Portão e acompanhar mais uma transformação importante da região. Desde 2020, construímos uma relação próxima com os moradores e entendemos que também precisamos evoluir junto com o bairro. Essa revitalização traz novos espaços, mais opções e novidades como a padaria sem glúten, mantendo aquilo que é essencial para nós: estar perto dos nossos clientes e fazer parte da rotina de quem vive no Portão” , afirma.

O Ítalo Portão está localizado na Rua João Bettega, 1040, com atendimento todos os dias. — Foto: Divulgação/Supermercados Ítalo.

Com o conceito “Ítalo Portão, ainda mais do seu jeito”, a unidade inicia uma nova etapa, com ambientes renovados e um conjunto de novidades que amplia as possibilidades de compras e alimentação para os moradores da região.

articles.title: After 38 years teaching in Massachusetts, Tufts math professor Loring Tu donated more than $10 million to the university in 2024, helping expand student aid
articles.summary: Loring Tu, a mathematics professor at Tufts University, donates over $10 million to enhance student financial aid, commemorating his grandfather Tsungming Tu, a pioneering Taiwanese educator and physician.
articles.body: A mathematics professor who spent decades teaching at Tufts University built his fortune through the stock market and later gave much of it back to the institution. According to the Taiwan Embassy, Loring Tu donated an eight-figure sum, worth more than $10 million, in honour of his late grandfather. In response to the gift, the university renamed its Science and Engineering Complex the Tsungming Tu Complex, after his grandfather. Tu had taught at Tufts for 38 years when the donation was announced and planned to retire at the end of 2025, and said he wanted the university to have greater financial resources for student assistance.A gift that is synonymous with family history Completed in 2017, the university’s Science and Engineering Complex brought together renovated older buildings with new construction. With facilities made to support collaboration across disciplines, it served the School of Engineering and the School of Arts and Sciences and saw its name changed in November 2024 following Loring Tu’s donation.According to the university’s record, Loring Tu’s grandfather, Tsungming Tu, was a Taiwanese physician, pharmacologist, and educator who was born in 1893 in Sanzhi, which is now part of New Taipei City. Coming from modest beginnings, he grew up in a family mired in financial hardships and, at the age of 10, saw his father, a tea farmer, pass away from injuries sustained in a field accident.In the year 1914, he graduated at the top of his class from Taiwan Governor Medical College, a forerunner of Taipei Imperial University Medical School. By 1922, he had completed his doctoral dissertation, equivalent to a PhD, at Kyoto Imperial University. In doing so, he achieved the feat of becoming the first Taiwanese professor to obtain a doctorate in medical sciences amid other professors who were mainly Japanese. Following World War II, he was named the first dean of National Taiwan University Medical School.Tsungming Tu would go on to create a lasting legacy for his innovative treatments for opium addiction and earned an appointment from the Japanese colonial government to tackle the problem. The list of his accomplishments continued, and he went on to establish an early opium addiction clinic in Taiwan and help curb the use of that drug. His epidemiological studies of the merits and demerits of snakebite were equally influential and groundbreaking.In 1954, he founded Kaohsiung Medical College, now Kaohsiung Medical University, Taiwan’s first private medical school to bridge the gap for Indigenous communities and people in remote villages who had limited access to doctors.Smart investing and giving back to TuftsBefore he donated to the university, Loring Tu had established two endowed scholarships and supported three on-campus houses that would benefit junior and senior students alike. The initiative came from his own personal experience, as Tu's life as a student was a success story made possible through financial aid. The financial aid had allowed him to study at McGill University and Princeton University and later secure a PhD at Harvard University.Tu joined the university faculty in 1986, and while he worked at Tufts, his academic work involved the study of manifolds, higher-dimensional counterparts of curves and surfaces. In addition, he had also authored or co-authored four books on geometry and topology, the mathematical study of spaces and shapes.According to the Boston Globe, it wasn’t wisdom from financial advisors that brought him financial success but rather a calculated purchasing of shares in company products he was familiar with. Led by his background in mathematics, Tu had invested in several well-known companies, particularly Apple, whose shares he had first bought in 1997. At the time, Apple stock was trading at around 15 cents a share, adjusted for splits, and a $1,000 investment made then would be worth well over $1 million today. Speaking on the experience, he remained modest and said, “I didn’t expect to be wealthy; I would attribute it mostly to dumb luck and frugality.”Although he had studied at Princeton and Harvard, he chose to give to Tufts partly because he believed his money could have a greater effect there. His donation was acknowledged by Tufts President Sunil Kumar, who said the gift would support the university’s teaching, research and learning for future generations. The donation also recognised a family connection that stretched from Tsungming Tu’s medical education work in Taiwan to his grandson’s career in American higher education.You use AI every day. articles.title: 25 noise complaints filed against Hindu temple: Anonymous neighbors fume over events at Fremont temple
articles.summary: A dispute has erupted between residents of a California neighbourhood and a large Hindu temple after locals complained about loud music, late-night events
articles.body: A dispute has erupted between residents of a California neighbourhood and a large Hindu temple after locals complained about loud music, late-night events and crowds gathering at the religious site, NBC Bay Area reported. The complainants wants to remain anonymous, the report said.Residents in the Bay Area have filed more than 25 noise complaints against the Fremont Hindu Temple, also known as Vedic Dharma Samaj, alleging that a series of events featuring loud music and people yelling have disrupted the neighbourhood.Video footage shared by a neighbour shows flashing lights and loud noise continuing beyond 9 pm, despite the absence of a special event permit at the time.In recent weeks, residents say they have faced another particularly noisy event, leaving them frustrated and struggling with their daily routines.“I could tell you that we have had issues with sleep. We have had problems waking up in the morning because these events sometimes go on for very late into the night and it’s been very frustrating,” one neighbour told NBC Bay Area anonymously.“We saw hundreds of people at 9:30 and the noise was still going on,” the neighbour said, describing a recent event organized by the temple.“The first week we moved in, there was almost like a concert-like setting in our neighborhood here,” another resident said.The temple had obtained a special event permit for the particular event, NBC Bay Area reported. However, residents alleged that the noise continued beyond the 9 pm deadline for amplified sound.The city said it had received complaints about the event and was investigating them.Residents want the temple to consider restricting the number of people attending its events.“City staff will continue coordinating with the temple and adjacent neighbors, monitoring activities and adjusting future permitted activities as appropriate to work toward constructive solutions to the issues that have been reported,” the city of Fremont told NBC Bay Area.Neighbours have also raised concerns about noisy events taking place during school hours.However, residents have clarified that they are not opposed to the temple organizing events. Their concern, according to the news station, is that the religious organisation should be more considerate about how these gatherings are conducted.“They’re drawing 10s of thousands of people, a more appropriate venue with proper permits would be more appropriate here,” one resident said.Videos and photographs shared on social media by the Fremont Hindu Temple show a range of events taking place at the site. Some posts feature gatherings with hundreds of thousands of people in attendance, while others show religious ceremonies involving music and offerings to different Hindu gods.According to its website, the Fremont Hindu Temple has been serving the Bay Area since 1985. articles.title: In 2026, near Esterbrook, Wyoming, 12 retired turbine-blade sections became an 8-foot snow fence and a 120-foot mustang mural; WYDOT will evaluate it this winter
articles.summary: In 2026, Esterbrook, Wyoming, saw an innovative solution for decommissioned wind turbine blades, transforming them into a snow fence and a stunning mural. This winter, WYDOT evaluates its effectiveness as a new way to recycle turbine waste.
articles.body: There is a lingering problem with clean energy: what to do with wind turbine blades when they reach the end of their working life. Made from durable composite materials, the blades are difficult to recycle and can extend for dozens of metres. In Wyoming, some retired blades have been buried or stockpiled, prompting efforts to find practical ways to reuse them.The physical snow fence was installed near Esterbrook in Converse County, Wyoming, in late 2025. In 2026, sculptor Chris Navarro and community volunteers painted 40 running mustangs across the 12 sections, transforming the structure into a 120-foot public art installation. The finished work, named Windborne, was dedicated on October 3, 2026. Its sections stand about 8 feet tall, while the full arrangement extends 120 feet. The artist’s official project page documents the installation’s dimensions and dedication. The Wyoming Department of Transportation will monitor its performance during the winter of 2026 to 2027 to determine whether it can effectively control drifting snow.Why old blades cause so much troubleThe difficulty of recycling retired blades has led to several disposal and reuse proposals. Wyoming passed House Bill 129 in 2020, directing the state to establish rules for using retired turbine materials in surface mine reclamation. In January 2025, the federal Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement approved an amendment to Wyoming’s regulatory programme allowing inert, decommissioned blades and towers to be used as backfill in approved areas of surface coal mines. The rule took effect on February 12, 2025. This limited use is subject to reclamation requirements; it is not a general approval to dispose of turbine materials anywhere in a mine.Casper sculptor Chris Navarro, who has worked professionally as an artist for about 40 years, began exploring artistic uses for retired turbine blades nearly six years ago after seeing a photograph of blades being buried. Separately, Jake Milne founded ReviablEnergy after seeing discarded blades at the Casper landfill and began looking for practical ways to reuse them. Their interests came together in Windborne, which combines Navarro’s artwork with the snow fence concept Milne wanted to test. Navarro has described the installation as his sixth idea for reusing a turbine blade.Building WindborneVestas donated a retired turbine blade and helped with the technical design. A Vestas engineer assisted with cutting the blade into sections and recommended how to space them. Twelve sections were selected and planted upright on private ranch land near Esterbrook, along Wyoming Highway 94, with ReviablEnergy helping to install them. The ranch owner agreed to host the test after the Wyoming Rescue Mission sought a snow fence to help keep its access road open during winter. The sections stand about 8 feet tall and are arranged across a total length of 120 feet. The length describes the full fence and mural, not the length of an individual section.The 12 sections represent the 12-step recovery process associated with the mission’s work with people experiencing addiction and homelessness. Navarro led painting workshops in Casper, and mission residents and community volunteers painted 40 running mustangs across the sections during the summer. A local wild horse adoption and training ranch also contributed. The finished work was dedicated on October 3, 2026, with about 50 people attending. Not everyone was pleased. A local pastor held a small protest at the entrance, called the sculpture a scam and said it spoils the view, and one other resident turned up in support of him. Navarro took the criticism calmly and said an artist cannot please everybody.What WYDOT will be observingThe mural is the most visible part of Windborne, but the main practical question is whether the sections can catch blowing snow before it reaches the road. WYDOT’s Winter Research Services team, established in 2004, studies blowing snow and advises on snow fence placement and winter road maintenance. Its work includes monitoring conditions during storms to understand how snow drifts form. The department’s Winter Research Services page explains the team’s role and the benefits of snow fences.Kathy Ahlenius, WYDOT’s winter research project manager, said the department had discussed using reclaimed turbine blades as snow fences before, but had not had funding for a test. She hopes the winter weather near Esterbrook will provide enough snow for the team to assess how effectively Windborne controls drifting. The sections may need less maintenance than conventional wooden fences, but their performance must be assessed under real winter conditions.Windborne’s artistic message is already visible, but its value as a snow fence remains to be tested. The winter monitoring will show whether the retired blade sections can control drifting snow while giving a difficult-to-recycle material another use. The installation brings public art and a practical engineering trial together, although its long-term effectiveness will depend on how it performs in real winter conditions.You use AI every day. articles.title: End of SIR doesn't mean freezing of voters list: SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said completion of special intensive revision (SIR) does not mean electoral rolls have been frozen, a statement that would
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday said completion of special intensive revision (SIR) does not mean electoral rolls have been frozen, a statement that would put to rest the apprehension that names removed from draft rolls cannot be restored to the voters' list and such persons are rendered permanently disabled from exercising their franchise.Hearing petitions challenging SIR in UP, Kerala and Chhattisgarh, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to extend the deadline. It said no extension was needed as inclusion of voters' names is a continuing process.Senior advocate D S Naidu said people could apply for inclusion even after SIR, with additions possible until nominations are filed for an election.EC, however, admitted lapses by UP officials in accepting bulk Form 7. It said corrective steps were taken and action was initiated against erring officials. SC allowed the petitioner to flag discrepancies to EC.EC said Kerala's SIR was completed in Feb and the last assembly polls were held using rolls prepared after it. CPM, through advocate G Prakash, said 24 lakh voters were still excluded. SC asked CPM to provide details of voters who could not submit enumeration forms because of insufficient time, enabling EC to examine the cases and take corrective action.Senior advocate Raju Ramachandran, appearing for another petitioner, alleged large-scale voter deletions during Kerala SIR and sought a comprehensive affidavit from EC despite completion of the process. articles.title: This Layla pillow gave me the side-sleeping support I’d been missing — now $119
articles.summary: I tested Layla’s BioCrystal Side Sleeper Pillow to see if its shoulder cutout and adjustable loft could improve my sleep. Here’s my honest review.
articles.body: I'm a side sleeper, no matter how hard I try to sleep on my back. Side sleeping isn't necessarily bad, but it's made it a challenge to find a pillow that cradles my head and neck without leaving me stiff or achy in the morning — until now. After sleeping on the Layla BioCrystal Side Sleeper Pillow, I finally found what I would consider to be the ideal setup for side sleepers. It's soft, yet supportive, and I've noticed a meaningful difference in my nightly comfort. Now through Nov. 26, FOX readers can get an extra 20% off the sale price of both BioCrystal pillows with code FOXDEAL. That brings the Side Sleeper Pillow down to $119 and the Classic Pillow to $111. Layla BioCrystal Side Sleeper Pillow: $119 (37% off) with code FOXDEAL Original price: $189 Side sleepers know how difficult it can be to find a comfortable position and stay there. Traditional pillows don't always provide enough support for your shoulder and neck, and can flatten throughout the night. Layla's BioCrystal Side Sleeper Pillow strikes a comfortable balance between softness and support. Its adjustable loft lets you choose among 7, 6 or 5 inches, while the U-shaped cutout gives your shoulder more room to rest naturally. Since I prefer to sleep slightly elevated, I've kept mine at the full 7-inch loft and find it to be the perfect height. My neck and shoulders melt into the U-shape (rather than being forced into an awkward position) and, better yet, continues to support me when I switch sides or roll onto my back throughout the night. The foam feels soft and responsive when I press into it, but it's firm enough to hold its shape under the weight of my head. I also appreciate that it doesn't feel overly dense. What is BioCrystal technology? According to Layla, BioCrystal technology infuses a blend of 16 natural crystals throughout the pillow's foam layers. The brand says the technology is designed to help regulate temperature and promote a more restorative sleep experience. I can’t speak to the effects of the crystals themselves, but I do notice that the pillow feels comfortably cool when I first lie down. It also doesn’t seem to trap as much heat as some memory foam pillows I’ve tried. The overall feel is soft, plush and lightly cooling. What you should know The pillow measures 16 by 23.5 inches, weighs 5.7 pounds and has an adjustable 5- to 7-inch loft. It fits standard pillowcases, but the U-shaped design makes a fully enclosed case — such as one with a zipper or fold-over closure — the best option. Pillowcases with one open end may slide out of place. I noticed a new-pillow smell, also known as off-gassing, during the first week or two. It has gradually faded, but shoppers who are sensitive to scents may want to air it out before using it. The cover is removable and machine washable. Layla recommends washing it in warm water on a gentle cycle with like colors and tumble drying it on low. Do not use bleach. The four foam layers should only be spot-cleaned and allowed to air-dry completely. Keep the foam out of the washer and dryer, since excessive water and high heat can damage its structure. My final thoughts The Layla BioCrystal Side Sleeper Pillow is a strong option for side sleepers who want structured support, a higher profile and the ability to adjust the height. The shoulder cutout gives it an advantage over traditional rectangular pillows, especially if you tend to wake up with neck or shoulder discomfort. Back and stomach sleepers may prefer the Layla BioCrystal Classic Pillow. My husband sleeps on it every night and appreciates its plush support, adjustable loft and roomy design, which keeps his head and neck comfortably supported when he’s lying on his back.

articles.title: An aquarium plant escaped into Florida waterways in the 1950s; within 40 years, hydrilla had spread to over 70% of the state’s watersheds
articles.summary: An aquatic plant imported for home aquariums became a major management problem in Florida after it entered the state’s freshwater systems in the 1950s.
articles.body: An aquatic plant imported for home aquariums became a major management problem in Florida after it entered the state’s freshwater systems in the 1950s. Hydrilla, a submerged plant native to parts of Asia, can grow rapidly, form dense mats near the water’s surface and spread through fragments carried between water bodies. Within about 40 years of its introduction, the plant had established populations in more than 70% of Florida’s watersheds, according to the University of Florida’s Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (UF/IFAS) guide, Hydrilla Integrated Management. The US Geological Survey (USGS) records Florida’s first observation in 1952 and says the plant is now established in 28 US states, as well as Guam and Puerto Rico. Its spread has complicated boating, threatened native aquatic vegetation and created a costly, ongoing challenge for waterway managers.How hydrilla spread across Florida after arriving as an aquarium plantThe UF/IFAS guide says the female, or dioecious, form of hydrilla reached Florida from Asia in the 1950s as an aquarium plant. An aquarium owner released it into a freshwater body in the Tampa Bay area. The USGS database also records that plants imported for aquariums entered Florida’s inland waters after being discarded or planted into canals in Tampa and Miami. The plant spread quickly. According to the UF/IFAS guide, hydrilla had established populations in more than 70% of Florida’s watersheds within 40 years of its introduction. Its distribution expanded from early records in the 1950s to much of the state by the 1990s.The Florida invasion involved the female form, which reproduces without needing a male plant. A separate form, known as monoecious hydrilla because individual plants have both male and female flowers, was first detected in the Mid-Atlantic region, including Delaware and the Potomac Basin. The USGS describes it as a separate introduction, while the UF/IFAS guide identifies Korea as its suspected origin. In its January 2026 revision, the USGS listed hydrilla as established in 28 states, in addition to Guam and Puerto Rico. Its database records the plant in 42 Florida drainage units, although a drainage-unit record does not necessarily mean that every water body in that area is infested. The USGS database records Florida observations from 1952 through 2026.Fast growth, fragments and underground tubers help hydrilla spreadHydrilla is a fast-growing submerged plant. The University of Florida’s plant directory reports growth rates of 1 to 4 inches per day. A 2012 study by Glomski and Netherland examined commonly cited growth rates and found that growth varied depending on whether researchers measured individual shoots or the expansion of the plant as a whole. The guide dates to 2014, so the experiment should not be interpreted as a newly conducted study. The plant can also grow in low-light conditions, requiring as little as 1% of full sunlight. It is frequently found at depths of around 9 feet and has been recorded at 45 feet in Kings Bay, Crystal River, Florida. Once the stems reach the surface, hydrilla forms a dense canopy that blocks light from reaching other submerged plants. The UF/IFAS guide says about 80% of its biomass is concentrated in the upper 2 feet of the water column.Its ability to reproduce through several routes makes control more difficult. Hydrilla spreads through stem fragments, underground tubers and buds known as turions. The guide says each tuber may produce a plant capable of generating several thousand new tubers per square metre. About 50% of fragments with just 1 whorl of leaves can regenerate into new plants. The USGS identifies recreational boats, motors, trailers and live wells as common ways hydrilla fragments reach new water bodies. Fragments can take root and establish new colonies, often near boat ramps. Tubers can also remain dormant in sediment for years, allowing infestations to return after visible growth has been removed.How hydrilla affects native plants, waterways and wildlifeDense hydrilla growth can crowd out native aquatic vegetation and interfere with waterway use. The USGS says its surface mats block sunlight from reaching native plants and can obstruct boating, swimming and fishing. Heavy infestations can also interfere with water withdrawals for irrigation and power generation. The UF/IFAS guide describes additional environmental effects. Dense growth can restrict water flow through rivers and canals, while the decay of plant material can contribute to sediment accumulation. Changes in light and oxygen conditions can affect other aquatic organisms. The guide also notes that hydrilla can provide a habitat for a cyanobacterium that produces a toxin associated with neurological disease in waterbirds, including bald eagles and American coots.The plant’s effects depend on the water body and the extent of the infestation. Its dense growth can provide habitat for some organisms while reducing the range of conditions available to others. Management therefore involves balancing access for people with the protection of native vegetation and aquatic ecosystems.Florida’s hydrilla control methods and costsFlorida uses a combination of physical removal, herbicides and biological controls to manage hydrilla. The UF/IFAS guide says the state spends millions of dollars each year managing the plant, but that figure is a broad estimate in a guide published in 2014, not a verified current annual expenditure. The guide’s estimated costs include $400 to $1,000 per acre for hand pulling and $100 to $500 per acre for herbicide treatments. These are historical estimates and should not be treated as current quotes. The guide also documents hydrilla populations resistant to the herbicides fluridone and endothall, highlighting the limitations of relying on chemical control alone.Biological control is another option. Triploid Asian grass carp, which are sterile, can be used to consume aquatic vegetation, but their possession and stocking are regulated and require the appropriate permits. Researchers have also studied insects that feed on hydrilla, although biological control does not necessarily eliminate an infestation. Florida’s Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) says a permit is generally required before people control or remove aquatic plants from state waters, unless a specific exemption applies. The agency also warns that possessing hydrilla in Florida without special permission is illegal.For boaters and aquarium owners, preventing further spread remains important. The FWC advises people to clean boats, trailers, live wells and gear before leaving a water body, and never to transplant hydrilla between waterways. Aquarium plants should never be released into lakes, canals or rivers. Preventing a small fragment from reaching a new water body can help avoid another expensive infestation.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2022, an Arizona woman hiked roughly 1,000 miles below the Grand Canyon’s rim alone; she completed the traverse in 77 days where no trail exists
articles.summary: In 2022, Jen Hogan made history as the first non-Native woman to complete a solo walk from rim to rim in the Grand Canyon, covering around 1,000 miles in 77 days without a trail, facing incredible challenges along the way.
articles.body: Most visitors explore the Grand Canyon along established trails or view it from the rim. In 2022, Jen Hogan, a Tucson-born National Park Service ranger, completed a solo, continuous traverse beneath the rim from Lees Ferry to Pearce Ferry, covering about 1,000 miles in 77 days. Grand Canyon National Park announced her achievement in a March 2022 post on its official Instagram account. A 2023 profile in Arizona Highways described Hogan as the first non-Native woman known to complete the journey, while noting that earlier Indigenous journeys may have gone undocumented. This was a continuous wilderness traverse beneath the rim, not a conventional rim-to-rim hike along established trails.A route with no trailThe Grand Canyon is often measured along the Colorado River, whose length through the park is listed by the National Park Service as 278 miles. Travelling below the rim on foot is a very different undertaking. Hogan had to climb in and out of side canyons, cross exposed ledges and locate water, covering far more ground than the river distance alone suggests. No continuous trail runs the entire length of the canyon below the rim. Instead, the traverse requires route finding through ledges, drainages and steep terrain.Hogan first visited the canyon with her grandfather when she was six or seven. She remembers asking him whether it was possible to go down into the canyon, and he told her it was impossible. As an adult, she built up her experience by hiking the route in shorter sections on both sides of the canyon. With help from Rich Rudow, fellow rangers and friends, she placed 5-gallon buckets of food and supplies at planned cache sites before setting out, allowing her to restock every five to 10 days. Her previous trips helped her identify water sources and difficult sections along the way.Two attempts that ended earlyHogan’s first attempt began on January 2, 2018, when she set out from Pearce Ferry. After about two weeks, a ledge gave way beneath her as she crossed a high route, sending her roughly 30 feet down. She initially thought her injuries were minor and continued hiking for several weeks before she was forced to stop at Parashant Canyon, around river mile 199. A medical scan in Flagstaff later showed that she had fractured her pelvis in six places.Hogan attempted the traverse again several months later, but pneumonia forced her to stop and spend weeks recovering at her brother’s home. A profile in Arizona Highways described her story as a cautionary tale. The risks of canyon travel remain clear in the National Park Service’s 2025 statistics: the park recorded 232 search and rescue incidents and 848 emergency medical service incidents that year. It also recorded 8,265 backcountry permits used. These are parkwide figures for 2025, not statistics from Hogan’s 2022 expedition.Finishing in 77 daysHogan’s third attempt began in the winter of 2021 and continued into 2022. This time, she started at Lees Ferry, where the higher elevation offered cooler starting conditions and water was more readily available. Because it turned out to be a warm winter, beginning at the eastern end made sense. Seventy-seven days later, she completed the traverse. Fellow ranger Della Yurcik met her at a ranger station with a hot pizza, a welcome meal after weeks in the canyon.Rich Rudow, who completed a 57-day traverse beneath the rim in 2015, understands the difficulty of the route. In Arizona Highways, he described travel below the rim as a test of judgment and adaptability because hikers must contend with weather, difficult terrain, limited water and their own health. He credited Hogan’s persistence and willingness to change plans with helping her succeed. Rudow’s account of his background and 2015 traverse confirms his own journey through the canyon.A 2023 profile in Arizona Highways reported that Hogan had been reassigned to Lees Ferry, where she would meet hikers and rafters near the starting point of her traverse. The profile also reported that she served in the Air Force before joining the National Park Service and earned three bachelor’s degrees and two master’s degrees. Hogan said she would attempt the traverse again if given the opportunity. Her achievement was a continuous solo journey below the rim, completed in 77 days after two earlier attempts ended in injury and illness.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Port Sudan families can barely afford water as shortages persist
articles.summary: Despite efforts to restore damaged infrastructure, residents face soaring water costs as war, displacement strain supply
articles.body:
Port Sudan, Sudan – Every day, Amina Khalafallah spends 10,000 Sudanese pounds ($1 at the parallel market rate) on water for herself and her four children. Over a 30-day month, that amounts to 300,000 pounds ($30) – the equivalent of her entire monthly salary.

Khalafallah lives in the Deim Mayo neighbourhood of Port Sudan, in eastern Sudan, where her home is not connected to a piped water network. Instead, she depends on street vendors, who charge 1,000 pounds ($0.10) for 18 litres.

Khalafallah works in a cafeteria at a private institution, while her husband works in another state and sends money to help her out when he can.

Between them, the family barely scrambles enough money to get by, but Khalafallah says she often has to borrow money. It’s a typical story in Sudan, where, according to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the country’s more than three-year-long war has pushed average incomes back to levels last seen in the early 1990s.

The hotter months bring additional challenges, as water prices rise and vendors become harder to find.

“We make sure to set aside money for water in the summer before covering our other household needs, even if that means going without some essentials,” Khalafallah told Al Jazeera.

According to the African Development Bank (AfDB), access to safe water is one of Sudan’s most urgent needs, with millions of children at risk of waterborne diseases.

In Port Sudan, relatively safe from the fighting that has plagued other areas of the country, the arrival of people displaced by the war has put additional pressure on already fragile infrastructure. The AfDB has reported that the city’s water supply was meeting less than 40 percent of demand.

One of the major issues Port Sudan has faced is the collapse of the Arbaat Dam. Located in the Red Sea Hills northwest of Port Sudan, it once supplied half of the coastal city’s daily water needs.

But in August 2024, heavy rainfall and flooding caused the dam to collapse, destroying villages downstream and damaging pipelines and wells.

As a result of the collapse , entire neighbourhoods are dependent on expensive water deliveries by truck.

Ahmed Osman, 30, has spent the past three years working at a water distribution station that supplies street vendors who deliver water to households.

When Sudan’s war began in April 2023, Osman said he charged vendors 4,000 Sudanese pounds ($0.40) to fill a donkey-drawn cart carrying at least 250 litres of water.

Those prices have since risen sharply, he said, because of increasing operating costs, particularly the fuel needed to transport water to his distribution station.

“A water tanker carrying 50,000 litres of water now costs 1.5 million Sudanese pounds [$150], compared with about 450,000 pounds before the war,” Osman told Al Jazeera.

Osman keeps the water in storage tanks before pumping it into the vendors’ carts. He charges 16,000 pounds ($1.60) to fill a cart carrying 250 litres.

After his expenses, Osman typically makes a profit of about 70,000 pounds ($7) per day, split between him and his partner.

Rehabilitation work has restored parts of the damaged water network.

According to the UNDP, the restoration work has included drilling or rehabilitating 15 boreholes, laying 17 kilometres (10.5 miles) of new pipelines, as well as installing solar-powered pumps.

The UNDP said the restored system could supply water to nearly 230,000 people.

However, that would still not be enough to supply water to all of Port Sudan, which the UNDP estimates to now have a population of one million people.

Other projects are therefore necessary to meet the water needs of residents – including one launched in June by the AfDB and UNICEF, which intends to expand access to safe water for up to 750,000 people in the city.

Emad Hafez, medical director of the emergency department at Port Sudan Teaching Hospital, told Al Jazeera the water crisis poses serious risks to public health, increasing the risk of waterborne diseases and making it harder for families to maintain basic hygiene.

He warned that disruptions to water supplies can force families to rely on untreated water, increasing the risk of cholera and other diarrhoeal diseases, particularly during the rainy season and in overcrowded displacement camps.

“Water shortages can also make it harder for families to maintain adequate hygiene, increasing the risk of skin infections and other hygiene-related illnesses,” Hafez said. “Meanwhile, storing water in uncovered containers can create breeding sites for mosquitoes, raising the risk of vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue fever.”

Water shortages also threaten healthcare services, Hafez said, explaining that hospitals require reliable supplies for infection prevention, cleaning and patient care.

“Beyond its immediate health consequences, water insecurity can worsen food shortages and malnutrition by disrupting agricultural activities and placing additional financial pressure on already vulnerable households,” he said. “Children under five and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to the effects of inadequate nutrition.”

A donkey-drawn cart, locally known as a ‘karo’ or ‘saqqa’, used to transport water in Sudan. Each cart carries about 250 litres [Fatima Edam/Al Jazeera]
Ahmed Osman works at a water distribution station supplying street vendors in the Deim Mayo neighbourhood of Port Sudan [Fatima Edam/Al Jazeera]

articles.summary: Ley de Rescate Económico del gobierno De La Espriella: estos son los cambios clave en IVA y renta
articles.body: El gobierno de Abelardo De La Espriella radicó oficialmente en el Congreso de la República el proyecto de Ley de Rescate Económico, una iniciativa fiscal de alto impacto que busca evitar una recesión, sanear las finanzas públicas y prevenir la pérdida de más de 360.000 empleos en el país. Con advertencias del vicepresidente José Manuel Restrepo sobre la necesidad urgente de "salvar a Colombia de la quiebra", la propuesta introduce modificaciones estructurales en materia tributaria, tarifas de IVA, renta para personas naturales y corporativas, así como una reducción drástica del gasto estatal. A continuación, presentamos un detallado abecé con los puntos clave que afectan directamente el bolsillo de los colombianos y el futuro de las empresas. La iniciativa tiene un doble propósito: ordenar las finanzas del Estado y reducir su tamaño en un 15 por ciento. Según el Ejecutivo, el gobierno anterior heredó una situación crítica que obliga a implementar ajustes inmediatos. Entre sus premisas destaca que el 10 por ciento de la población con mayores ingresos asumirá el equivalente al 9 por ciento de los recursos esperados con la reforma. 1. Tarifas y eliminación de exenciones 2. Devolución y compensación del IVA Para mitigar el impacto en los hogares de menores ingresos: 3. Compras por internet del exterior (menores a US$ 200) Todas las adquisiciones realizadas en plataformas de comercio electrónico internacionales deberán pagar IVA sin importar su monto, una medida orientada a proteger el comercio y la industria nacional. Reducción de renta corporativa: La tarifa general de renta para las empresas bajará al 33 por ciento en 2027 y se ubicará en el 31 por ciento a partir de 2028. articles.title: Polish president turns back from Senegal trip as top court chief suspended
articles.summary: WARSAW, Poland — Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned back his plane en route to Senegal on Friday after police entered the premises of Poland‘s top court and its president was suspended.
articles.body: WARSAW, Poland — Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned back his plane en route to Senegal on Friday after police entered the premises of Poland‘s top court and its president was suspended. “At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland. I am cutting short my flight to Senegal. I am returning,” he said on X. Police said officers entered the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal after incidents outside the court, including the throwing of dangerous objects at police. The tribunal said on its website that the court’s president, Bogdan Swieczkowski, had been suspended on Friday. A long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralyzed the institution. Earlier this year, Nawrocki, an ally of Poland‘s former nationalist government of the Law and Justice or PiS party, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski, who was a deputy justice minister under PiS, declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties. Restoring the rule of law is the government’s duty, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on X later on Friday. “After years of lawlessness under PiS, this process is difficult, at times even painful, and requires decisive action. There is no other way,” he said. Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek told reporters he has requested the lifting of the immunities of Swieczkowski and his deputy for failing to fulfill their duties by preventing judges from performing their work. PiS politicians, including leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski, said Tusk’s government was carrying out a coup on the tribunal.

articles.title: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.summary: Sanctioned Russian FM attends Atlanta talks as Iran war, Hormuz disruption and Ukraine divide G20 members.
articles.body:
The United States has scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

The move exposes deep rifts at the heart of the Group of 20 (G20), whose foreign ministers are meeting in the southern city of Atlanta in the United States for talks overshadowed by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.

“There will be no family photo featuring our European partners together with Mr Lavrov,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, according to the dpa news agency.

Lavrov, who remains under Western sanctions imposed after Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, arrived in Atlanta ahead of the talks, Russian state media reported. Moscow said on Thursday that he would use his speech to argue against international sanctions. Ukraine was not invited, the Abu Dhabi-based newspaper The National reported.

A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Russia’s presence at the G20 “in no way legitimises its actions”.

The European Union’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas pledged on Thursday to urge G20 partners to strengthen support for Ukraine and pursue accountability through a special tribunal and claims commission, after a Russian strike on a Ukrainian railway station killed at least 14 people earlier that day.

The meeting also comes weeks after US President Donald Trump issued sanctions waivers allowing Russia to export diesel to ease fuel prices before the November 3 midterm elections.

Opening the talks, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged members to cooperate on economic and geopolitical crises threatening global trade, energy and food supplies, and freedom of navigation, dpa reported. Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz after US-Israeli strikes began in late February, and global energy prices have risen sharply since.

“Both maritime and food security drive economic security,” Rubio wrote on X.

No joint statement is expected. A diplomatic source told the AFP news agency that Washington will instead publish a chair’s summary it has drafted. The source added: “The G20 is no longer really a forum where foreign ministers can reach agreement on a statement.”

No government has said whether Rubio and Lavrov will hold a formal bilateral meeting.

China sent Executive Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu in place of Foreign Minister Wang Yi, according to a delegation list released by the Department of State. South Africa, a founding G20 member, has been excluded by Washington, and the African Union is represented by Burundi’s Edouard Bizimana.

The Atlanta talks are the last ministerial meeting of the US G20 presidency before leaders meet in Miami on December 14 and 15.

articles.title: Meta settles claims with second plaintiff in social media addiction case
articles.summary: Meta on Friday reached a settlement with a teen plaintiff, identified in court documents as K.D.B., who claimed the company’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, were addictive and caused her mental ‌health problems, attorneys for the plaintiff said.
articles.body: Meta on Friday reached a settlement with a teen plaintiff, identified in court documents as K.D.B., who claimed the company’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, were addictive and caused her mental ‌health problems, attorneys for the plaintiff said. The news comes just one day after the tech giant reached a settlement with S.J., the second teen plaintiff who had sued the company over similar claims. The terms of the settlement agreements with both plaintiffs are confidential. In the weeks leading up to trial, TikTok and YouTube reached agreements to resolve the claims brought against them by both S.J. and K.D.B. “We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client,” Emily Jeffcott, trial counsel for K.D.B., said in a statement. Snap Inc. now remains the lone defendant in the trial, which began this week in Los Angeles with jury selection. Opening arguments are slated for Nov. 4. In their lawsuit, K.D.B. and S.J. allege that Snap, the maker of Snapchat, designed features that would maximize the time young users spend on the app. Those features include Snapstreaks, Snapscores and filters that can trigger compulsive use of Snapchat, leading to severe mental and physical health issues like self-harm. Their case is the fourth bellwether in a consolidated group of cases brought against Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Snap by more than 1,600 plaintiffs, including over 350 families and over 250 school districts. The plaintiffs accuse the tech companies of knowingly designing addictive products harmful to young users’ mental health. Historically, social media platforms have largely been shielded by Section 230, a provision added to the Communications Act of 1934 that says internet companies aren’t liable for the content users post. Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, has repeatedly denied that its apps are purposefully harmful and addictive for young users. In March, during a landmark social media addiction trial in Los Angeles, a jury found Meta and Google’s YouTube negligent in the design or operation of their social media platforms. The jurors determined that Meta’s and Google’s negligence was a substantial factor in causing harm to the plaintiff, identified in court by her initials, K.G.M., and that the companies failed to adequately warn users of the dangers of Instagram and YouTube, their respective platforms. The jury awarded K.G.M. $3 million in compensatory damages, finding Meta 70% responsible for harm caused to the now-20-year-old plaintiff, and YouTube responsible for 30%. In August, Meta agreed to settle a wide-ranging social media addiction lawsuit with the state of California and a number of other states for about $18 billion. The court filing says that the company “denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs,” which are a collection of 29 states. In a statement to NBC News on Friday, a spokesperson for Meta said the company will continue to defend itself in court and stand by its record. “We’ve spent more than a decade building protections for teens, and our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general goes even further with strict time limits, no access at night, and no notifications during school hours,” the statement read in part. “We hope the rest of our industry joins us in setting this new standard.” A spokesperson for Snap on Friday sent NBC News its statement from earlier this week, which read, in part, “From the beginning, Snapchat was built differently from traditional social media: it opens to a camera, not a feed, not a ranking of what other people post or other social comparison metrics.” “We have built safeguards into the platform, introduced safety tools and educational resources,” the statement continued, “and we believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed.”
