articles.title: ICE agent charged for allegedly striking a Mexican national with his car
articles.summary: The Mexican national, who was living in the US without legal documentation, suffered multiple leg fractures and a hip injury, prosecutors said.
articles.body:
A US immigration agent has been charged with felony for allegedly hitting a man with a vehicle earlier this month in Texas, a prosecutor announced.

The prosecutor said US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer Mario Alberto Morales was indicted by a grand jury on a charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

Morales is accused of running over a Mexican national who was living in the US without legal documentation, leaving him with multiple leg fractures and a hip injury.

An ICE spokesperson dismissed the indictment as "nothing more than a political stunt" and described the allegations as "reckless and false".

The indictment comes amid the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration and a series of violent incidents involving federal agents that have resulted in injuries and deaths.

If convicted, Morales faces between two to 20 years in prison for the second-degree felony, according to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare.

Teare said Morales pursued a vehicle driven by Miguel Parra-Hernandez, a 48-year-old Mexican national who has lived in Texas for more than 30 years without legal documentation, on the morning of 10 October.

Parra-Hernandez and another occupant fled the vehicle on foot before Morales "aggressively steered his vehicle" into the Mexican national, Teare said at a news conference in Houston on Friday.

He said Parra-Hernandez had no criminal record and was not subject to a deportation order.

"Not only did he hit Mr Hernandez, he ran over both of his legs, leaving him seriously injured and hospitalised to this day," Teare said.

Morales then called 911 to report that Parra-Hernandez had hit his car.

Teare said that ICE was allegedly pursuing a man named Jose Mendoza-Cervantes, a Mexican national and undocumented immigrant, who has apparently been dead for nine years.

Immediately after the incident, an ICE spokesperson told the BBC's US media partner CBS News that Parra-Hernandez had run in front of the immigration agent's vehicle.

Following the indictment, ICE rejected the allegations brought by the grand jury - a panel of citizens empowered to determine whether there was sufficient evidence to bring criminal charges.

"This is nothing more than a political stunt by Houston sanctuary politicians," an ICE spokesperson said in a statement to the BBC.

"Allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE," the spokesperson said, adding that the men and women of ICE "are entrusted with upholding the rule of law and are held to the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, and ethical conduct".

The statement added that federal officers acting in the course of their duties could only be investigated by other federal agencies. The spokesperson insisted that local governments did not have the authority to run such an investigation.

District Attorney Teare stressed that he had the utmost respect for law enforcement and believed that undocumented individuals who were violent felons should be deported.

He said he hoped the prosecution would not only deliver justice for Parra-Hernandez and his family but also send "a loud and clear message to every ICE officer who feels that they have a free pass to terrorise our streets".

articles.title: Lèse majesté: Arnon Nampa questioned Thailand's monarchy dressed as Harry Potter. Now he's in jail for 34 years
articles.summary: Thailand has prosecuted 294 people since 2020 under its lèse majesté law, with sentences going up to 50 years.
articles.body:
Even before they come through the door, you can hear the prisoners walking towards the courtroom, the shackles round their ankles clinking with each step.

The five who walk into the courtroom are familiar with the routine; they are facing multiple criminal prosecutions and have spent much of the past five years going back and forth to court.

One of them, a small, bespectacled man with greying hair, opens his arms to hold his three-year-old son, who has been brought to court by his partner to see him.

This is Arnon Nampa, a 42-year-old human rights lawyer. His offence was to call for Thailand's powerful monarchy to be scrutinised and held accountable. He did this dressed as the eponymous young wizard at a Harry Potter-themed demonstration in central Bangkok in 2020.

On Friday a court in Bangkok sentenced him to two years and eight months for violating Thailand's lèse majesté law, or article 112, under which more people have been jailed for perceived insults against the royal family than in all the other countries that have such laws combined.

This is just one out of 14 cases brought against Arnon under the same charge, bringing the cumulative sentence he has received so far to more than 34 years. The verdict in two cases is still pending.

"To me, this isn't a surprise," he later told reporters. "If the country was more open, we would be able to talk about these issues freely."

The past six years have seen the most extensive use of lèse majesté in Thai history, in response to unprecedented student protests in 2020 which for the first time called for a public discussion of the role of the monarchy. Two hundred and ninety-four people, including 20 under the age of 18, have been prosecuted, receiving prison sentences of up to 50 years. Dozens of them are still on trial.

Most of those charged under this law are denied bail and kept in jail, even though their court cases can last several years. The standard defence of the law given by Thai officials is that it "reflects the culture and history of Thailand, where the monarchy is one of the main pillars of the nation, highly revered by the majority of Thai people".

Article 112 of the Thai criminal code simply reads, "Whoever defames, insults or threatens the King, the Queen, the Heir-apparent or the Regent, shall be punished with imprisonment of three to 15 years."

In practice, though, the law has been interpreted to cover a much wider range of comment about the monarchy, and a much wider range of figures. Saying anything negative about any member of the royal family, about the institution of the monarchy, even about long deceased kings, or in one case, the king's dog, has resulted in prosecutions.

"If you ask me what the text of the law says, I can tell you," says Akarachai Chaimaneekarakate, assistant director of Thai Lawyers for Human Rights, which helps defend those accused of breaking it. "If you ask me how the courts interpret the words "defame" or "insult", I don't think I can give you a definition, because it's so ambiguous, it's so vague. Even questioning the law itself, for example, can constitute lèse majesté under Section 112."

From his cell in the Bangkok Remand Prison, where he has been for the last three years, Arnon has been writing to his young daughter and son.

"Dear Pran and Karl, my beloved children

The winter wind has not only brought us cool weather, but also brings back stories from the past. I miss the time we travelled outside Bangkok that first winter after Karl came into this world. It was such a magical time for me. I shall miss it every winter I spend here until I regain my freedom."

Hearings like the one Arnon attended weeks before Friday's verdict are the only times he has seen Karl since he was a baby.

Karl is shy at first, but soon he's happy to be picked up and shown off to the other prisoners. His 10-year-old sister Pran sometimes visits their father in prison, and often draws and paints him.

But Arnon and Lookwa, his partner, think Karl is too young to visit. For now, Karl thinks the court is just where his dad works. A group of supporters has come too, filling the little courtroom. They mingle cheerfully with the prisoners, laughing and exchanging gossip before the judges walk in to start the hearing. It is an improbably informal setting for men facing one of the most feared charges in Thailand.

The effect of the law has been to smother any public discussion about the monarchy. Until six years ago, opinions on it were only ever whispered in private. In one notorious case a taxi driver was jailed because a passenger reported what he had said while riding in his cab.

That year younger Thais had become increasingly frustrated with the conservative government led by coup-leader Gen Prayuth Chan-ocha. The year before millions had given their votes to a new party, Future Forward, which promised sweeping reforms, but in February 2020, the Constitutional Court dissolved the party on a technicality. The arrival of the Covid pandemic prevented any protests for three months, but as infections in Thailand started to fall, students began holding rallies calling for an end to the military's role in politics. Arnon Nampa argued this did not go far enough.

In the garb of Harry Potter, he gave a speech saying it was time to talk about the opaque power and wealth of the monarchy. He criticised King Vajiralongkorn's decision to take personal control of the vast assets held by the Crown Property Bureau, and over important units of the army.

In a single speech Arnon shattered a taboo which had hung over Thai society for the whole of its modern history. For the rest of that year the student-led protests continued, with increasingly bold demands for changes to the monarchy.

At the time, the use of the lèse majesté law had been suspended for three years. Sources close to the palace have in the past acknowledged that the negative publicity generated by lèse majesté convictions might do more harm than good.

But the protests forced a hasty reassessment. From the end of 2020 prosecutions under the law restarted and accelerated. Dozens of young activists have fled into exile to avoid being jailed.

One of them is Supitcha "Melinn" Chailom. The 24-year-old from Chiang Mai in northern Thailand lives in Montreal, a fugitive from four 112 charges which have been filed against her.

She was an 18-year-old school girl when she stood up and made a speech at a protest in Chiang Mai University, just three weeks after Arnon Nampa's call for reform of the monarchy.

A local photographer captured the moment she raised her hand in the three-finger Hunger Games salute, eliciting loud cheers from the crowd. It became one of the defining images of the protests, and propelled Melinn to nationwide fame.

She travelled up and down the country as one of the leading voices in the movement, demanding changes to Thailand's old-fashioned education system, conducting polls on what people thought of the monarchy.

"I love playing games, and I dreamed of being a game designer," she told me from Canada. But her parents did not approve.

"I felt that, as a young person, I could not question, or have a discussion with people older than me. The monarchy gave me the same vibe."

In November 2020 Melinn joined a protest in the southern city of Hat Yai, where she gave a speech comparing the royal treatment given to the king's dog with that of ordinary people. Nine months later the police delivered a summons to her home charging her with lèse majesté.

"It was a shock. I wasn't expecting it because I only talked about the dog. It was during Covid when the police came to my home with the summons, so they knew my parents would be there with me. They tried to stay calm, but I nearly lost my mind."

Her family tried to persuade her to co-operate with the authorities, to admit her wrongdoing. But Melinn refused.

She joined a movement calling itself Thalu Wang, which translates as "breaking through the palace". Instead of giving speeches, they came up with stunts like holding polls on the street, asking people what they thought of royal motorcades holding up the traffic, or whether they believed the monarchy had too much power.

"We knew the risks, but we thought it would be safer just conducting a poll. It turns out it was not."

She was given two more lèse majesté charges in 2022, and detained before being released on bail. She had to wear an electronic monitor on her ankle and was barred from leaving her home between 4pm and 6am. Her parents were forced to sign a document promising to inform on her. She was facing decades in jail.

Melinn decided she had no choice. With a friend she fled Thailand and eventually got asylum in Canada.

Article 112 is on paper just a law, like any other, passed by Thai parliament, which can, theoretically, be amended by elected MPs. In fact it has been amended in the past, notably in 1976 when the punishment for breaking it was increased to between three and 15 years in prison.

But today the Constitutional Court has decreed that the law itself, like the institution it protects, is untouchable. The reformist Move Forward party - the successor of Future Forward - was dissolved in 2024, and its leader banned from politics, merely for proposing that the punishments be less harsh. And the courts make it very difficult for those charged under it to defend themselves.

"In many cases, like the one against Arnon Nampa, prosecutors accuse the defendant of lying about the monarchy," says Chaimaneekarakate, the lawyer. "But when we ask the judge to subpoena documents or witnesses who could show the truth of what the defendant says, the judge refuses to do it. When one lawyer protested against the court deciding that the trial would be held in secret, she was warned by the judge to be quiet or face a contempt of court charge."

He says judges sometimes criticise the young activists over their alleged actions even before the trial has started.

As the one who ignited the debate about the monarchy Arnon appears to be getting the harshest punishment. Despite the formidable odds stacked against him he still prepares carefully for every court appearance, taking part in his own defence and helping other inmates with theirs.

This isn't easy; he is not allowed to bring any of his written notes, and must memorise all his arguments.

The judges object to him playing the part of a lawyer in his regulation-brown prison shorts, his feet bare and shackled. But it does give him an opportunity to see his family.

The letters he writes are the only other way he stays in touch with them. He may spend his entire life in prison. He wants his children to know him, and to understand, when they are older, why he chose to challenge the system and lose his freedom.

"Since the first day that we made up our mind to take up this mission, we knew of the dangers. Speaking the truth is not difficult. What is difficult is speaking a forbidden truth. I remember well that on the evening of 3 August 2020, after speaking at the Harry Potter event, I felt very good, content, and relieved to have finally begun speaking about the truth, in public," he wrote to his family last year.

Earlier this year, he wrote: "Living here is a struggle. But it is just a dot in the bigger picture of our movement's struggle. We must play a part in writing our own history. Become a drop of water that will one day become an ocean."

articles.title: Panchang Today, October 31, 2026: Krishan Paksh 6 (Shashthi), Ardra, Shubh Muhurat, Rahu Kaal and More

articles.body: Panchang Today is that steady daily guide many of us lean on, whether we’re rushing to work, planning a family get together, or simply trying to keep our mind calm. It’s rooted in the spiritual wisdom of the Hindu calendar, where the Moon’s mood, the star of the day, and key time windows help you act with more precision. A good Panchang day feels like walking with a small lamp in the hand, you still choose the road, but you see the bumps sooner. Staying connected to our cultural roots also helps us make mindful decisions. Below are the important Panchang details for October 31, 2026 for India:Date & Day DetailsOctober 31, 2026 falls on a Saturday, and the lunar tone is set by Krishan Paksh 6 (Shashthi). Shashthi in Krishna Paksha carries a disciplined, corrective energy. The Moon is past the early waning phase and now encourages tidying up what’s messy, fixing what’s broken, and facing small responsibilities you’ve been postponing. This tithi ends at 16:57:34, after which Krishan Paksh 7 (Saptami) begins. So the first part of the day suits repairs, review, and honest conversations. The later part, after 16:57:34, begins to feel a little more action oriented, but only if you’ve done the groundwork.The nakshatra is Ardra, lasting until 07:12:03, and then it moves into Punarvasu. Ardra is associated with storm energy, intense thought, and clearing. Its presiding deity is Rudra, a fierce form of Shiva, known for dissolving what has become stale. That’s why Ardra mornings often feel mentally busy, sometimes restless, even a bit edgy. Words can come out sharp if you’re not careful. Yet it’s also excellent for research, problem solving, deep cleaning, and cutting away distractions. After 07:12:03, Punarvasu begins, and the emotional weather softens. Punarvasu is linked with renewal, return, and simple goodness. It helps you rebuild after the clearing, like fresh green shoots after a heavy rain.The Moon sign is Gemini 19.19 for most of this date, which brings quick thinking, conversations, messages, and that “mind jumping from one tab to another” feeling. Useful for networking, writing, and studying. Less useful for staying steady on one long task unless you structure your day well. The Moon sign transitions at 01/11/2026 00:00:48 into Cancer, shifting the mood from head to heart. Late night becomes more emotional and home focused, so keep late conversations gentle.Yoga is Siddha until 17:31:47, followed by Sadhya. Siddha supports success through skill and right method. Do the work properly and results follow. It’s not a lazy luck type of day. Karan also shapes the rhythm. Gara Karan lasts till 06:08:44, then Vanij continues until 16:57:34, followed by Visti. Vanij is linked with trade and practical dealings, good for routine office work, purchases that are necessary, and getting paperwork in order. Visti, which begins after 16:57:34, asks for extra care. Keep things simple in the evening. If you must take a decision, sleep on it, then finalise tomorrow.Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Auspicious timings today arrive like clear patches between passing clouds. If you use them well, the day feels far smoother.Brahma Muhurta runs from 2026-10-31 04:22:38 to 2026-10-31 05:13:50. This is the quietest part of the day, when the mind is less tangled and prayer lands deeper. Meditation, japa, study, or even writing your plan for the day works beautifully here. If you’ve been meaning to restart a habit, start in this window. Small beginnings taken seriously.Pratah Sandhya is from 2026-10-31 04:48:14 to 2026-10-31 06:05:02. It’s ideal for Surya arghya, a bath, and settling your breath. This time supports clarity and good intentions. Keep your phone away for a bit, let the morning be yours.Abhijit Muhurta falls at 2026-10-31 11:19:06 to 2026-10-31 12:03:58. Think of it as a balancing point in the day, good for important calls, submitting applications, signing routine documents, or meeting someone to resolve a misunderstanding. Not for ego battles. For clean closure.Vijay Muhurta is from 2026-10-31 13:33:42 to 2026-10-31 14:18:34. If you need to push a stuck task forward, present your case, or ask for support from a senior, this is your window. Your boss will notice when you speak with facts and calm confidence.As evening arrives, Godhuli Muhurta runs from 2026-10-31 17:17:53 to 2026-10-31 17:43:29. This twilight time is sweet for lighting a lamp, a short prayer, and family togetherness. Sayahana Sandhya continues from 2026-10-31 17:17:53 to 2026-10-31 18:34:41, suitable for evening worship and a peaceful transition from work mode to home mode.Ravi Yoga lasts from 2026-10-31 07:12:50 to 2026-11-01 05:39:50. It supports steady progress and confidence, especially after the Ardra to Punarvasu shift. Nishita Muhurta is from 2026-10-31 23:16:17 to 2026-11-01 00:07:29, traditionally strong for deep spiritual practice. Amrit Kalam appears at 2026-11-01 03:25:08 to 2026-11-01 04:54:56, a nourishing window for prayer and inner reset.Choghadiya also offers helpful cues. During the day, look to Shubh @ 07:29, Laabh @ 13:05, and Amrit @ 14:29 for smoother outcomes. At night, Laabh @ 17:17, Shubh @ 20:29, Amrit @ 22:05, and Laabh @ 28:29 support good momentum, especially for study, planning, or calm family time.Inauspicious TimingsRahu Kaal today is from 08:53 to 10:17. This period is treated as unpredictable for fresh starts because Rahu amplifies confusion, shortcuts, and mixed signals. If you can, avoid launching a new project, making a big purchase, signing contracts, or locking in a financial commitment in this window. Keep your wallet closed today, at least during Rahu’s hours. Use the time for routine tasks, filing, cleaning, and simple follow ups.Rahu Kaal is also a powerful time for inner work. Sit quietly for a few minutes, do pranayama if it suits you, and chant the Rahu mantra, Om Raam Rahave Namaha. If you feel anxious, don’t feed it with more screen time. Step outside, drink water, and slow your speech. Ardra energy in the morning can make people talk fast and cut corners. Don’t.The detailed inauspicious timings include rahu_kaal from 2026-10-31 08:53:14 to 2026-10-31 10:17:21. Gulika Kaal is listed as gulkai_kaal from 2026-10-31 06:05:02 to 2026-10-31 07:29:08. Gulika is linked with delays and avoidable detours, so don’t schedule your most important meeting right at the start of the workday if you can help it. Ease into the day, finish basics first.Yamaganda runs from 2026-10-31 13:05:33 to 2026-10-31 14:29:40. This is another period best kept for routine work, not for starting something you want to grow fast. Dur Muhurtam is from 2026-10-31 07:34:46 to 2026-10-31 08:19:46, a classic warning slot for avoidable friction. If you’re commuting then, drive patiently. If you’re in a family discussion, don’t raise your voice.Varjyam appears from 2026-10-31 18:26:50 to 2026-10-31 19:53:11. Varjyam is like a temporary dip in supportive energy. Avoid confrontations and avoid pushing for approvals in this time. Let people breathe. Baana (Nripa) stretches from 2026-10-31 06:05:02 to 2026-10-31 21:17:02, reminding you to act with dignity and restraint. It’s a long influence, so keep your conduct clean, especially in public spaces and online.Two more combinations are mentioned. Vidaal yoga runs from 2026-10-31 06:05:02 to 2026-10-31 07:11:50, suggesting some caution in the early morning. Aadal yoga follows from 2026-10-31 07:12:50 to 2026-11-01 05:39:50, and it can make the mind restless if you keep piling tasks. Work in blocks, not in a scattered rush.Choghadiya inauspicious periods also deserve attention. In the day: Kaal @ 06:05, Rog @ 08:53, Udveg @ 10:17, and Kaal @ 15:53. At night: Udveg @ 18:53, Rog @ 25:17, and Kaal @ 26:53. If you must act in these, keep it simple and double check details. No impulsive commitments.Rahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal varies across India because it is calculated using local sunrise, and sunrise shifts from place to place due to longitude differences. That’s why one time can’t fit the whole country. The table below shows Rahu Kaal for major Indian cities, helping you plan your key tasks in your own location without guesswork.CityRahu KaalMumbai09:30 - 10:56Delhi (NCR)09:18 - 10:41Bengaluru09:08 - 10:35Hyderabad09:06 - 10:33Chennai08:57 - 10:24Ahmedabad09:33 - 10:58Pune09:25 - 10:51Kolkata08:30 - 09:55Jaipur09:22 - 10:46Kochi09:11 - 10:40Lucknow09:02 - 10:26Indore09:20 - 10:45Guwahati08:18 - 09:42Chandigarh09:20 - 10:43Surat09:31 - 10:56Visakhapatnam08:47 - 10:14Nagpur09:06 - 10:31Coimbatore09:09 - 10:37Varanasi08:53 - 10:17Bhubaneswar08:38 - 10:04Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise is at 06:05:01 and sunset is at 17:17:59. These two times are the spine of the day, around which all other rhythms settle. A sunrise prayer, even a simple namaskar with folded hands, helps align the mind with discipline, which suits Saturday’s serious tone. If you’re stepping out early, pause for a breath at 06:05:01 time range, it sets a steadier pace for the hours ahead.Sunset at 17:17:59 carries a natural invitation to slow down. With Godhuli Muhurta beginning at 2026-10-31 17:17:53, the evening turns spiritually supportive. Light a diya, keep the home calmer, and let arguments wait for another day.Moonrise is at 10:07:46 PM, and moonset is at 12:19:27 PM, Nov 1. A late moonrise often makes the mind more active at night, especially with the Moon still in Gemini for most of the date. You may find yourself thinking about conversations, unfinished replies, and tomorrow’s plans. Write down what you must remember, then let it go. After the Moon sign transitions at 01/11/2026 00:00:48 into Cancer, emotions can feel closer to the surface. Keep night time gentle. A little prayer before sleep will help you wake up lighter.Vrat/Festival Information & RecommendationsNo major Vrat or festival is observed today. The Hindu month context still matters, though. In the amanta month, it is Ashvina, while in the purnimanta month, it is Kartika. This junction feeling, Ashvina’s closing mood and Kartika’s devotional pull, often nudges people to clean up habits and make space for steadier routines. That’s the inner theme of the day too.On the personal front, Ardra early morning can make tempers short and words sharper than intended. Someone at home may ask a simple question and it may sound like pressure. Pause. Answer slowly. After 07:12:03, when Punarvasu begins, warmth returns and it becomes easier to reconcile. If you’ve been meaning to check on an elder, or to speak to a sibling without bringing old baggage, do it in the late morning or afternoon. Keep it real, keep it kind.Work and career matters benefit from the Siddha Yoga that lasts till 17:31:47. This is the kind of day where good method beats raw speed. Put your priorities on paper. Clear pending emails, tidy your desk, update a document that has been lying half done. If you’re studying, break it into two or three focused sessions. Gemini Moon supports learning, but only if you stop multitasking. And during Rahu Kaal from 08:53 to 10:17, avoid new launches or big promises. Handle routine tasks, proofread, and do the quiet groundwork.Money matters need a sober eye. Saturday already asks for restraint, and the waning Moon prefers thoughtful spending. Buy what’s needed for the home, but don’t shop out of boredom. If you’re tempted to place a quick order or make an impulse payment, wait till Abhijit Muhurta at 2026-10-31 11:19:06 to 2026-10-31 12:03:58, or even better, sleep on it.For spiritual practice, keep it simple and consistent. If you can, use Brahma Muhurta from 2026-10-31 04:22:38 to 2026-10-31 05:13:50 for japa or meditation. In the evening, use Godhuli Muhurta from 2026-10-31 17:17:53 to 2026-10-31 17:43:29 to light a lamp and offer a short prayer. It’s not about doing a lot. It’s about showing up.Carry this one guiding rule through the day: do fewer things, do them properly. Keep your speech calm in the morning, guard your focus in the afternoon, and make your evening quieter. Actionable advice for today, choose one important task to complete before 16:57:34, avoid starting anything new in 08:53 to 10:17, and end the day by switching off screens 30 minutes early and doing a short chant of Om Raam Rahave Namaha.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Queensland’s Kuridala copper town prospered during World War I, but a 1918 cyclone damaged its smelter before the plant closed in 1920
articles.summary: Kuridala, about 65–70 km south of Cloncurry in Queensland, grew into an important copper-mining settlement before and during World War I.
articles.body: Kuridala, about 65–70 km south of Cloncurry in Queensland, grew into an important copper-mining settlement before and during World War I. Its development was closely tied to the Hampden Smelter and a railway connection that helped transport ore from the surrounding mining district. But the town’s prosperity depended on the copper industry, leaving it exposed to changing prices, operational disruptions and financial pressures. Queensland Places records Kuridala’s population at about 1,500 in 1913 before reporting 774 by 1921. The Queensland Heritage Register gives different figures, recording a population of 2,000 by 1920 and 800 by 1924.How the Hampden Smelter and railway helped build KuridalaKuridala developed through several name changes. The Queensland Heritage Register records that the settlement was surveyed as Hampden in 1910 and known as Friezland by 1912 before officially becoming Kuridala in October 1916. Queensland Places gives an earlier sequence that begins with Gulatten, followed by Friezland and Kuridala. According to the Heritage Register, the final name was intended to avoid confusion with another Queensland settlement, although anti-German sentiment has also been suggested as a possible factor during the war. Railway development and copper processing were central to the town’s growth. The railway reached Cloncurry in 1908, with an extension serving the Hampden area opening in 1910. The Hampden Smelter began operating in March 1911 and continued until 1920, allowing copper ore from nearby mines to be processed locally. The smelter helped support a substantial settlement, with businesses and public services developing around the mining industry.By 1913, Kuridala had about 1,500 residents, according to Queensland Places. The town had hotels, shops, an ice works, a printery, a hospital, churches and a school. These facilities reflected the needs of a community whose employment and commercial activity were closely connected to mining and smelting. World War I sustained the region’s prosperity rather than initiating Kuridala’s growth. The Queensland Heritage Register describes the conflict as bringing four years of prosperity to the Cloncurry district and notes that the period was particularly prosperous for the company operating the smelter. Queensland Places identifies 1918 as a high point for the settlement. It records a daily school attendance of 280 children, while the Heritage Register describes the school as having up to 280 pupils.Why Kuridala declined after World War IKuridala’s fortunes changed as the conditions supporting copper production weakened. British wartime price controls ended in 1918, and the Queensland Heritage Register says the change forced the company into difficulties. In December 1918, a cyclone damaged the smelter and its powerhouse. Smelting was postponed until September 1919. The plant processed about 69,598 long tons of ore in 1920, equivalent to approximately 70,715 tonnes, according to the Heritage Register. The smelter’s closure was also connected to financial difficulties. The Heritage Register records that the Commonwealth Bank withdrew funds against copper awaiting export, after which the company halted all operations. Queensland Places also identifies the collapse in copper prices in 1920 as a factor in the town’s decline.Population figures from the period differ between the sources. Queensland Places reports 774 residents by 1921, while the Heritage Register records 2,000 by 1920 and 800 by 1924. As mining and smelting activity contracted, facilities that had supported the settlement were moved elsewhere. The hospital, picture theatre and courthouse were relocated to Mount Isa, while the ice works also followed. The Queensland Heritage Register records that the company ceased to exist in 1928, after offering its assets for sale in 1926 and their subsequent purchase by Mount Elliott.Kuridala today: the heritage significance of the Hampden SmelterThe remains of the Hampden Smelter are central to Kuridala’s historical significance. The Queensland Heritage Register identifies the site as evidence of the copper industry that helped shape the Cloncurry district. Its surviving industrial remains also have research potential for understanding the technology, organisation and operation of early 20th-century copper smelting. Kuridala’s history records the rise of a mining settlement supported by railway access and industrial investment, followed by the contraction of its principal industry. The surviving smelter remains, and historical records document the town’s place in Queensland’s copper-mining history.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: California transplants in Texas are voting Democrat, and they see no irony in it
articles.summary: California to Texas migration is reshaping Texas politics as Democratic transplants bring progressive values to the once ruby red McKinney, Texas.
articles.body: McKinney, Texas, is ground zero for the migration of voters from California to Texas over the past several years. On Election Day, it is these newcomers who may well tip the balance not just in the Senate and governor's races. They may also decide whether the once ruby red Lone Star State will continue to grow bluer. I met Oren at The Celt on the picture-postcard town square, where we played a friendly game of pool. He moved from California about a year ago "because it’s a lot cheaper to live" but is voting for Democrats because he believes that Texas needs "more social services and public transit" and more support for transgender kids. When I gently tried to press Oren on the apparent illogic of moving away from a high-tax, big-government blue state for reasons of cost only to vote to make his new home a high-tax, big-government state, he was unmoved, almost arguing that real California progressivism has never been tried. FOX NEWS POLL: TEXAS SENATE RACE GALLOPING TOWARD A PHOTO FINISH It turns out that Oren was not as much of an outlier as I had expected because, not long after, I met Daniel, who works at a local restaurant and moved to McKinney a few years ago with his best friend and girlfriend to start a business. He has also proudly brought his politics with him. "It’s in the Constitution," Daniel told Fox News Digital. "We can go anywhere we want. It's meant to be that way." When I asked him if he could understand why so many people born and raised in Texas are worried about transplants changing its politics, he shrugged and said, "Things change." JOE ROGAN WARNS LIBERALS AGAINST TRYING TO TURN TEXAS BLUE, SAYS IT WOULD WRECK THE STATE'S 'DELICATE BALANCE' In the space of about five hours, I met two more refugees from California prepared to keep voting for Democrats. Like Oren and Daniel, they really did not see any irony in the fact that they may be recreating in Texas exactly the conditions they escaped in California. The natives, however, do see the problem with the Californication of Texas. Terry, a longtime local in her 60s, told me, "I love to see the growth, and there’s a lot of it, but if they bring Democratic politics with them, then we stand to lose the whole thing bringing people here." Clint, who was in town from his home just on the other side of the Oklahoma border, is worried not just about Texas turning blue through domestic migration, but even about the Sooner State eventually turning blue. TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS; NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK "I cannot comprehend why someone would move from a state because there’s high taxes and then come down here and vote for high taxes. I just can’t comprehend it," Clint told Fox News Digital. "And I’ve asked them to explain it to me, but they just cuss me out." Thankfully, nobody cussed out this columnist for asking, but Clint is correct that the liberal transplants see no problem with transforming the red states they arrive in into blue states, and it's not just Texas. Arizona and even Montana have seen influxes of liberal California voters. West Virginians have similar fears regarding their neighbors to the south in Northern Virginia, who are also attracted by the low taxes and cost of living. ELECTION DAY 2026: JOIN AMERICA'S CONVERSATION HERE! In Texas, there is a kind of double-pincer political invasion because, along with the Cali converts, unchecked immigration — illegal and otherwise — over decades has also pushed the needle left in the state. This is, in a nutshell, the new Democratic Party coalition: wealthy, college-educated Whites and immigrants. The bottom line for Republicans — not just in Texas but in many red states — is that Americans are moving at stunning rates to cheaper states, which almost always means Republican states. The good news is that red states stand to gain in the Electoral College and in Congress after the next census, but that won’t matter if Democrats take them over. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Between now and then, and especially on Tuesday, "Don’t you turn my red state blue" has to be the mantra of the GOP. If Texas falls this time, then anywhere can, and that is exactly what the Democrats moving to red states are hoping for and creating.

articles.title: Selma Blair apologizes to the ‘people that I dissapointed’ after plane incident arrest
articles.summary: Selma Blair has spoken out publicly for the first time since her arrest on assault charges after an incident on a plane earlier this month, apologizing to “the people that I disappointed.”
articles.body: Selma Blair has spoken out publicly for the first time since her arrest on assault charges after an incident on a plane earlier this month, apologizing to “the people that I disappointed.” The 54-year-old “Cruel Intentions” star shared a video on Instagram on Friday, saying that though her attorneys advised her against speaking about the case, she’s taking the legal matter “very seriously.” “To the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed, I am so sorry,” Blair said. In the opening of her video, Blair said, “I know I’ve been quiet for a couple weeks since October 11th, and you deserve to hear from me directly. And I’m sorry that it’s taken this long.” Blair was on a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to New York City when she allegedly became “physically abusive” and was removed from the plane, authorities in New York said at the time. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital, Port Authority said. The actor was charged with two counts of second-degree assault related to her alleged actions after the flight. She is accused of kicking a Port Authority police officer who took her to the hospital and a nurse at the hospital later. She pleaded not guilty to those charges. In her video, Blair defended her character, saying it’s not her nature to harm others. “What I can tell you, though, is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself, and that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone a day in my life,” Blair said. She thanked those who reached out with love and support. “It has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as is Scout, who is also OK,” she said, referring to her service dog. “So right now, I’m going to be taking care of my health and my son, and thinking of you all with gratitude and love,” she said, concluding her video. Blair revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disorder that attacks healthy cells in the central nervous system, according to the National Institutes of Health. Blair’s attorney stated in court that her actions were the result of a medical emergency, citing diagnoses of multiple sclerosis and Parkinsonism. At her Oct. 12 arraignment, her attorney, Shawn Barnes, told the judge that he doesn’t believe the assault was intentional and that the star had missed several doses of medication and also fell and hit her head on the flight. Blair’s representative separately said in a statement that Blair had “experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct.” The case was adjourned until Jan. 19, the DA’s office said.
